To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ER and growth factor signaling intersect and directly interact, at every level of the signal transduction cascade.
the ERalpha and ERbeta isoforms are expressed differentially in breast tissue and that they have distinct biological properties.

estrogen and growth factors interact to regulate breast cancer cell growth through multiple mechanisms, which include cross-talk between ERalpha and the epidermal growth-factor-receptor (EGFR) and insulin-like growth-factor-1 receptor (IGF1R) pathways, and that the resulting synergism between estrogen and growth factors is a critical determinant in breast cancer progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms of cross-talk among ER, epidermal-growth-factor receptor (EGFR), and insulin-like growth-factor receptor (IGFR) signaling in normal mammary epithelial cells and in human breast cancer cells.
the mechanisms by which estrogen receptor (ER) action in breast cancer cells is modulated by other growth factors.
the mechanisms of cross-talk among the estrogen receptor, epithelial growth factor, and the insulin-like growth factor receptor pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERalpha and ERbeta have the potential to interact with all growth-factor-signaling molecules, but the exact nature and extent of these interactions are still not well understood.

the ER and growth factor signaling interact in many ways, at many levels, and in many cell types, but that the precise molecular mechanisms of cross-communication between ER and growth factor pathways are only beginning to be elucidated.
ER action in the breast is highly complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ERalpha and growth-factor-signing pathways are integrated in the nucleus by ERalpha, which is a master regulator of the transcription of genes that encode growth-factor-signaling components and their regulators.
ER and growth factor signaling pathways are not only parallel pathways but also intersect and interact with each other.
the growth factor signaling pathways are important for ER function, and ER is a critical regulator of growth factor signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ER and growth-factor signaling pathways intersect at every level of transduction and that the cross-talk between these pathways is a major determinant of breast cancer progression.

ER and growth-factor signaling interact at multiple levels and that the resulting synergistic effect of ER and growth factors is a key factor in breast cancer development, progression, and resistance to endocrine therapy.
the ER is not just a transcription factor.
